Ah, thank you for the correction! That makes complete sense now. 

`COUNT(email)` counts only non-NULL values in that column, whereas `COUNT(*)` counts every row regardless of NULL values. So the 20-row difference tells you exactly how many users in your table have NULL (missing) email addresses.

This is an important distinction to keep in mind—if you want to count all rows, use `COUNT(*)`. If you want to count only rows where a specific column has a value, use `COUNT(column_name)`.
